bull.b: The long-term power purchase agreement materially improves Phase 1 development visibility by securing a substantial electricity supply through 2047. Reliable contracted power is strategically important for attracting data-center tenants and supports the company’s broader plan to build a scalable digital infrastructure platform.

Owning a large, controlled site while expanding planned capacity creates a platform for multi-phase growth rather than a single project opportunity. The available acreage and stated master plan can support future customer capacity, improve development flexibility, and strengthen the strategic value of the Texas project.

Cash on hand and available project financing provide resources to advance permitting, construction preparation, and Phase 1 equity needs without relying entirely on immediate operating revenue. This funding runway supports execution over the next several quarters, although access to some facility tranches remains milestone-dependent.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated a self-funding operating model: revenue is small and declining while losses and cash outflows remain substantial. Continued burn can consume liquidity before projects generate revenue, increasing dependence on financing and making successful project execution essential to future financial stability.

The large equity issuance strengthens near-term funding but materially expands the share base, diluting existing holders and signaling continued reliance on external capital. Additional project financing, debt, or equity may be needed as development scales, potentially limiting shareholder economics if operating cash generation remains delayed.

The project’s value depends on converting permits, commercial agreements, leases, and financing conditions into construction and delivered capacity. An unexecuted PPA or regulatory delay could postpone tenant commitments and the targeted 4Q 2027 readiness date, extending the period before the project produces meaningful revenue.
